research_question: Does the frozen official G-reasoner checkpoint respond to relation fields it consumes, while preserving consistent relation-ID relabel invariance and the FK graph structure contract?
experiment_tier: synthetic mechanism and compatibility gate; exploratory, not downstream SQL main-line evidence

predecessor_failed_run.root_cause: PyG Data.to()/Data.cpu() mutate the same Data object; run_001's round-trip validation moved the inference graph back to CPU.

recovery_change: Clone the graph before moving it to the device; use a second clone for CPU round-trip verification so the graph passed to the model remains on the target device.

hypotheses.negative_control_C1: Changing only edge_attr/custom FK metadata with a bijective instance-ID relabel leaves output within epsilon.
hypotheses.relation_channel_C2_or_C3: At least one of edge_type or rel_attr perturbations changes output by more than epsilon.
hypotheses.semantic_relabel_C4: Consistent relation-ID and rel_attr-row relabeling leaves output within epsilon.

decision_rule.pass: C1 <= epsilon AND C4 <= epsilon AND (C2 > epsilon OR C3 > epsilon)
decision_rule.no_go: C1 <= epsilon AND C4 <= epsilon AND C2,C3 <= epsilon
decision_rule.stop: C4 > epsilon, invalid structure/shape/non-finite output/checkpoint mismatch, resource overrun, or execution failure
decision_rule.c5_c6: report anchor/query sensitivity as mechanism fingerprints only; not a SQL-aware method result

cases.change: frozen synthetic fixture, query and anchor
exact repeat to measure numerical noise
edge_attr plus bijective FK-instance relabel; consumed model inputs unchanged
swap paired forward/inverse edge_type role IDs; rel_attr fixed
permute paired relation-feature rows; edge_type fixed
